title: Full isolation of the ARC execution wall on the ONE clean navigation game (tu93): perception + goal are correct; the wall is obstacle-aware pathfinding within the move budget.
methodology_note: Source extraction (authorized offline dev, REQ-ARC-WMTE-5836 workflow) established navigation_only per game. tu93 is the ONLY navigation-only game of the 4 (sc25 needs spell-casting, ls20 needs attribute-morphing, cn04 needs endpoint-pairing). On tu93 with source-confirmed colors (player=9, exit=14 at logical (46,46)), ran: (a) the E3 value-head-routed explorer A/B, (b) a direct greedy-toward-exit navigator. No LLM. Public-game source read for offline dev only, never in the hidden submission.

findings.why_e3_ab_nulled: The 3 games the E3 perception-target A/B ran on (sc25/ls20/cn04) are all NON-navigation games -- no player->exit heuristic can solve them. The one navigation game (tu93) was SKIPPED because the mover detector missed its player.
findings.mover_detector_bug: detect_mover's max_shift=4.0 rejects tu93's player, which JUMPS ~6 logical cells per action (coarse grid). Raising/relativizing max_shift would recover it. This is why tu93 got mover=None and was skipped.
findings.root_cause: tu93 is a MAZE (color-2 rails, 288 cells) with a MOVE BUDGET (game-over ~26 moves). The E3 novelty-explorer nudged by the value head navigates PARTWAY (60->12) but does not close the gap around obstacles; greedy-toward-exit bounces off rails (~0.7 net progress/step despite 6-cell jumps) and times out. Neither does obstacle-aware pathfinding within budget.
findings.carnot_already_has_the_engine: Carnot's OfflineSolver (verifier-routed best-first search over replay-from-reset) ALREADY solves tu93 to L5 (ops/arc_solve_registry.yaml) using a hand-built GameAdapter's player->goal Manhattan verifier. The E3 LIVE explorer (force_explore) uses a WEAKER novelty-search that does not. The perception fix provides AUTONOMOUSLY (detect player 9 + exit 14 from frames) exactly what the hand-built GameAdapter provides MANUALLY.

headline: EXECUTION WALL FULLY ISOLATED. Perception is fixed and the goal is correct; the wall is a goal-directed OBSTACLE-AWARE PATHFINDER to the perception-detected target within the move budget. The E3 novelty-explorer is the weak link -- it navigates partway (tu93 60->12) but cannot close the gap around a maze within budget. Carnot's OfflineSolver verifier-routed best-first search ALREADY solves tu93 (registry L5) with a hand-built adapter's player->goal verifier -- so the concrete next capability is to feed the AUTONOMOUS perception-detected player+target as that verifier into the OfflineSolver-style search on the live path, replacing the hand-built GameAdapter.
next_capability: A perception-grounded verifier-routed navigator: (1) fix detect_mover max_shift for multi-cell-jump players (recover tu93-class players); (2) feed the detected player->target Manhattan as the OfflineSolver verifier (the mechanism that already solves tu93/L5), NOT the E3 novelty-explorer; (3) measure discovery on the navigation games. This is the honest, scoped build the full isolation earns.
